Class NetworkManager

java.lang.Object
NetworkManager
public class NetworkManager extends Object
Manages the TCP connection between two players. Wraps a socket with typed send/receive methods so the rest of the codebase never touches raw streams. All messages are line-delimited text sent in a fixed order, both sides must read exactly what the other side writes, in the same sequence.

  • Method Details

    • sendSetup

      public void sendSetup(String msg)
      Sends the color assignment to the client during setup. Called only by Server, exactly once, before the game starts.
      Parameters:
      msg - "WHITE" or "BLACK" — the color assigned to the client

    • readSetup

      public String readSetup()
      Blocks until the server's color assignment message arrives. Called only by Client, exactly once, before the game starts.
      Returns:
      "WHITE" or "BLACK", or null if the connection dropped

    • sendMove

      public void sendMove(int fromRow, int fromCol, int toRow, int toCol)
      Sends a move to the opponent as a comma-separated string: "fromRow,fromCol,toRow,toCol"
      Parameters:
      fromRow - row of the piece being moved (0 = top)
      fromCol - column of the piece being moved
      toRow - row of the destination square
      toCol - column of the destination square

    • receiveMove

      public int[] receiveMove()
      Blocks until the opponent sends a move. Called by GameRunner's listener thread in a loop for the entire game.
      Returns:
      int[4] of {fromRow, fromCol, toRow, toCol}, or null if the opponent disconnected

    • sendModifierOptions

      public void sendModifierOptions(Modifier.Type[] options)
      Sends the three modifier options that were offered to the local player. The opponent's GameRunner reads and discards these — they only need to know what was chosen, not what was offered.
      Parameters:
      options - array of exactly 3 modifier types to send

    • receiveModifierOptions

      public Modifier.Type[] receiveModifierOptions()
      Blocks until the opponent sends their three modifier options. Called by the listener thread immediately after receiving a move that triggers a modifier offer. The result is discarded — the listener only calls this to drain the message from the stream.
      Returns:
      array of 3 Modifier.Types, or null if connection dropped

    • sendModifier

      public void sendModifier(Modifier m)
      Sends a fully serialized modifier so the opponent can reconstruct it. Format: "type,turnsRemaining,pieceRow,pieceCol,affectedRow,affectedCol" pieceRow/pieceCol are -1 if the modifier has no piece target. affectedRow/affectedCol are -1 if the modifier has no square target.
      Parameters:
      m - the modifier chosen by the local player

    • sendModifierData

      public void sendModifierData(Modifier.Type type, int turnsRemaining, int pieceRow, int pieceCol, int affectedRow, int affectedCol)
      Sends raw modifier fields directly, used when a Modifier object is not available (e.g. when forwarding already-parsed data). Format is identical to sendModifier().
      Parameters:
      type - the modifier type
      turnsRemaining - turns until the modifier expires
      pieceRow - row of the targeted piece, or -1 if none
      pieceCol - column of the targeted piece, or -1 if none
      affectedRow - row of the targeted square, or -1 if none
      affectedCol - column of the targeted square, or -1 if none

    • sendResurrectionData

      public void sendResurrectionData(Piece piece, int row, int col)
      Sends a resurrection modifier with the extra fields needed to reconstruct the revived piece on the opponent's board. Appends the piece's type and side to the standard modifier format.
      Parameters:
      piece - the piece being resurrected
      row - row where the piece will be placed
      col - column where the piece will be placed

    • receiveModifier

      public NetworkManager.ModifierData receiveModifier()
      Blocks until the opponent sends a modifier, then deserializes it into a ModifierData record. Does not create any Piece objects — GameRunner resolves pieces from the board using pieceRow/pieceCol.
      Returns:
      a ModifierData with all fields populated, or null if the connection dropped or parsing failed

    • getIsWhite

      public boolean getIsWhite()
      Returns if the player is white
      Returns:
      true if the player is white, false if not

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes the underlying socket. Called when the game ends or the opponent disconnects.
